rationale:
Split into 3 children. The supplied proof (steps 1–5) contains three separable, reusable obligations about a single L-Lipschitz graph piece A over P (|(y−z) − p(y−z)| ≤ L|p(y−z)| on A):
- (A) graph_hausdorff_bound covers step 1 and the Lipschitz image bound of step 4: H^n(A) ≤ (1+L²)^{n/2} H^n(p(A)) for every such A, with no measurability or closedness.
- (B) graph_projection_null_measurable covers step 2: p(A) is H^n-null-measurable when A is.
- (C) graph_piece_fibre_bound covers steps 3–5 for one piece and depends on A and B: ∫⁻_A g dH^n ≤ (1+L²)^{n/2} ∫⁻_{P.plane} Σ_{y∈A, p(y)=a} g(y) dH^n(a) for arbitrary g : ℝ^N → [0,∞].

The parent keeps the countable gluing of steps 3–4, using only C. It was checked in Lean.
1. Pieces. Let A_i := G ∩ disjointed Γ i = (G ∩ Γ_i) ∖ ⋃_{j<i} Γ_j. These are pairwise disjoint (disjoint_disjointed). They are null-measurable, since G is and each disjointed Γ i is Borel (MeasurableSet.disjointed of the closed Γ_j). A_i ⊆ Γ_i, so A_i inherits the graph inequality. ⋃_i A_i = G by iUnion_disjointed and G ⊆ ⋃Γ_i.
2. Splitting the integral. ∫⁻_G g = Σ_i ∫⁻_{A_i} g by lintegral_iUnion₀, which holds for arbitrary g.
3. Per-piece bound. Apply C to each A_i, then pull out the constant with ENNReal.tsum_mul_left.
4. Recombining. Σ_i ∫⁻_{P.plane} F_{A_i} ≤ ∫⁻_{P.plane} Σ_i F_{A_i}, by countable superadditivity of the lower integral (le_lintegral_add on partial sums, ENNReal.tsum_eq_iSup_nat, lintegral_mono). The snapshot has no Mathlib lemma for this, so the glue proves it inline in about 10 lines.
   - This replaces the supplied lintegral_tsum because the order is swapped: C takes the supremum over simple functions for each piece. The per-piece fibre sums of an arbitrary g need not be a.e.-measurable; superadditivity needs no measurability.
5. Fibres. For every a, Σ_i F_{A_i}(a) ≤ F_G(a), by ENNReal.tsum_sigma and ENNReal.tsum_comp_le_tsum_of_injective for (i, y) ↦ y. That map is injective because the A_i are disjoint. Only the '≤' half of the step-3 bijection is needed.

subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of an L-Lipschitz graph piece is at most (1+L²)^{n/2} times that of its projection
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, P ∈ G(N,n) with orthogonal projection p := Grassmannian.project P onto the n-plane P.plane, L ≥ 0, and let A ⊆ ℝ^N be an L-Lipschitz graph over P, i.e. |(y − z) − p(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ A (A need not be closed or measurable). Then H^n(A) ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2} H^n(p(A)), where H^n = μHE[n] is the Euclidean Hausdorff (outer) measure on ℝ^N and the constant is ENNReal.ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2}).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (P : Grassmannian N n) (L : ℝ) (A : Set (Euclidean N)), 0 ≤ L → (∀ y ∈ A, ∀ z ∈ A, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) A ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + L ^ 2) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)) * (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) (Grassmannian.project P '' A)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (geometry of one graph) and the Lipschitz image bound used in step 4 of the parent proof (step B6 (iii)–(iv) of the proof of Simon 8.5.9), specialised to a single graph piece A; no closedness or measurability of A is used. Notation: H^n := μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, an outer measure, so H^n(S) is defined for every set S); p := Grassmannian.project P, the orthogonal projection onto the n-plane P.plane = range p; it is linear (p = P.projectionLinearMap), symmetric (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric) and idempotent (Grassmannian.project_project). A set S ⊆ ℝ^N is an L-Lipschitz graph over P when |(y − z) − p(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ S; every subset of such a set is again one.

1. Pythagoras for p. For v ∈ ℝ^N, symmetry and idempotence give ⟨p v, p v⟩ = ⟨p(p v), v⟩ = ⟨p v, v⟩, hence ⟨p v, v − p v⟩ = 0 and, expanding |p v + (v − p v)|² (norm_add_sq_real), |v|² = |p v|² + |v − p v|².

2. Inverse-Lipschitz estimate on A. Let y, z ∈ A and v := y − z, so p v = p(y) − p(z) by linearity. The hypothesis gives 0 ≤ |v − p v| ≤ L|p v|, hence |v − p v|² ≤ L²|p v|², and by step 1 |y − z|² = |p v|² + |v − p v|² ≤ (1 + L²)|p(y) − p(z)|². Taking square roots, |y − z| ≤ (1 + L²)^{1/2} |p(y) − p(z)|.

3. Injectivity and the inverse map. If y, z ∈ A and p(y) = p(z), step 2 gives |y − z| ≤ 0, so y = z: p is injective on A. Let h := Function.invFunOn p A. By injectivity h(p(y)) = y for every y ∈ A (Set.InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn), and therefore h(p(A)) = A (Set.LeftInvOn.image_image).

4. h is K-Lipschitz on p(A) with K := (1 + L²)^{1/2} (as an element of ℝ≥0: Real.toNNReal √(1 + L²)). Indeed, for a = p(y) and b = p(z) with y, z ∈ A, step 3 gives h(a) = y, h(b) = z, so by step 2 dist(h(a), h(b)) = |y − z| ≤ K|p(y) − p(z)| = K·dist(a, b) (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul).

5. Lipschitz image bound. By Mathlib's LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le (exponent d = n ≥ 0) applied to h on p(A), μH[n](h(p(A))) ≤ K^n·μH[n](p(A)); by step 3 the left side is μH[n](A). In [0, ∞], K^n = (ofReal √(1 + L²))^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(√(1 + L²)^(n:ℝ)) = ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2}) (ENNReal.ofReal_rpow_of_nonneg, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.rpow_mul). So μH[n](A) ≤ ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2})·μH[n](p(A)).

6. Normalisation. By definition μHE[n] = c·μH[n] with the constant c = addHaarScalarFactor volume μH[n] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, Measure.smul_apply). Multiplying the inequality of step 5 by c gives H^n(A) = c·μH[n](A) ≤ c·ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2})·μH[n](p(A)) = ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2})·H^n(p(A)). ∎
proof_key_steps: Pythagoras for the orthogonal projection: |v|² = |p v|² + |v − p v|².
Graph inequality ⇒ |y − z| ≤ (1 + L²)^{1/2}|p(y) − p(z)| on A; hence p is injective on A.
h := invFunOn p A satisfies h(p(A)) = A and is (1 + L²)^{1/2}-Lipschitz on p(A).
μHE[n] = c·μH[n] transfers the bound to H^n.

subproblems.title: The projection of a null-measurable L-Lipschitz graph piece is H^n-null-measurable
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, P ∈ G(N,n) with orthogonal projection p := Grassmannian.project P, L ≥ 0, and let A ⊆ ℝ^N be an L-Lipschitz graph over P (|(y − z) − p(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ A) that is H^n-null-measurable, H^n = μHE[n]. Then p(A) is H^n-null-measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (P : Grassmannian N n) (L : ℝ) (A : Set (Euclidean N)), 0 ≤ L → (∀ y ∈ A, ∀ z ∈ A, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖) → NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) → NullMeasurableSet (Grassmannian.project P '' A) (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (transfer of measurability and of null sets) of the parent proof (step B6 (iii)–(iv) of the proof of Simon 8.5.9), specialised to a single graph piece A. Notation: H^n := μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, an outer measure, so H^n(S) is defined for every set S); p := Grassmannian.project P, the orthogonal projection onto the n-plane P.plane = range p; it is linear (p = P.projectionLinearMap), symmetric (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric) and idempotent (Grassmannian.project_project). A set S ⊆ ℝ^N is an L-Lipschitz graph over P when |(y − z) − p(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ S; every subset of such a set is again one. The hypothesis 0 ≤ L is not used.

1. p is injective on A. If y, z ∈ A and p(y) = p(z), then p(y − z) = p(y) − p(z) = 0, and the graph inequality gives |(y − z) − 0| ≤ L·0 = 0, so y = z. Hence p is injective on every subset of A.

2. p is 1-Lipschitz. For v ∈ ℝ^N, symmetry and idempotence give |p v|² = ⟨p v, p v⟩ = ⟨p(p v), v⟩ = ⟨p v, v⟩ ≤ |p v|·|v| (Cauchy–Schwarz, real_inner_le_norm), so |p v| ≤ |v| (trivial if p v = 0; otherwise divide by |p v|). Thus dist(p(y), p(z)) = |p(y − z)| ≤ |y − z|, i.e. LipschitzWith 1 p; in particular p is continuous.

3. Borel/null decomposition. Since A is H^n-null-measurable, there is a Borel set B₁ ⊆ A with B₁ = A H^n-almost everywhere (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). Put Y := A ∖ B₁; then H^n(Y) = 0 (ae_eq_set), A = B₁ ∪ Y, and p(A) = p(B₁) ∪ p(Y).

4. p(B₁) is Borel. B₁ is a Borel subset of the Polish space ℝ^N and p is continuous (step 2) and injective on B₁ ⊆ A (step 1). By the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn) the image p(B₁) is Borel. (This is the Borel half of step 2 of the parent proof; there, when A lies in a closed graph Γ, the same conclusion is obtained by writing p(B₁) = {a ∈ p(Γ) : h(a) ∈ B₁} with the inverse h continuous on the closed set p(Γ).)

5. p(Y) is H^n-null. By Mathlib's LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with K = 1 and d = n, μH[n](p(Y)) ≤ 1^n·μH[n](Y) = μH[n](Y). Multiplying by the normalising constant c of μHE[n] = c·μH[n] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def) gives H^n(p(Y)) ≤ H^n(Y) = 0.

6. Conclusion. p(A) = p(B₁) ∪ p(Y) is the union of a Borel set and an H^n-null set, hence H^n-null-measurable (MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet, NullMeasurableSet.of_null, NullMeasurableSet.union). ∎
proof_key_steps: The graph inequality makes p injective on A.
p is 1-Lipschitz (|p v|² = ⟨p v, v⟩ ≤ |p v||v|), hence continuous.
Split A = B₁ ∪ Y with B₁ ⊆ A Borel and H^n(Y) = 0.
Lusin–Souslin: p(B₁) is Borel (p continuous and injective on B₁).
1-Lipschitz image bound: H^n(p(Y)) ≤ H^n(Y) = 0; so p(A) = p(B₁) ∪ p(Y) is null-measurable.

subproblems.title: Graph inequality on a single null-measurable L-Lipschitz graph piece, for arbitrary [0,∞]-valued integrands
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, P ∈ G(N,n) with orthogonal projection p := Grassmannian.project P, L ≥ 0, A ⊆ ℝ^N an L-Lipschitz graph over P (|(y − z) − p(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ A) that is H^n-null-measurable, H^n = μHE[n], and g : ℝ^N → [0,∞] arbitrary (not necessarily measurable). Then ∫⁻_A g dH^n ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2} ∫⁻_{P.plane} (Σ_{y∈A, p(y)=a} g(y)) dH^n(a), where ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral and the inner sum is the [0,∞]-valued sum (tsum) of g over the subtype {y : y ∈ A ∧ p(y) = a}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (P : Grassmannian N n) (L : ℝ) (A : Set (Euclidean N)) (g : Euclidean N → ℝ≥0∞), 0 ≤ L → (∀ y ∈ A, ∀ z ∈ A, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖) → NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) → ∫⁻ y in A, g y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + L ^ 2) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)) * ∫⁻ a in (P.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), (∑' y : {y : Euclidean N // y ∈ A ∧ Grassmannian.project P y = a}, g y) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 (fibres of one piece), 4 (Borel simple integrands) and 5 (arbitrary g) of the parent proof (step B6 (iii)–(iv) of the proof of Simon 8.5.9), for a single graph piece A. Uses the sibling results graph_hausdorff_bound (Lean: Submission.intcpt_graph_hausdorff_le_projection; H^n(S) ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2} H^n(p(S)) for every L-Lipschitz graph S over P) and graph_projection_null_measurable (Lean: Submission.intcpt_graph_projection_nullMeasurableSet; p(S) is H^n-null-measurable for every H^n-null-measurable L-Lipschitz graph S over P). Notation: H^n := μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, an outer measure, so H^n(S) is defined for every set S); p := Grassmannian.project P, the orthogonal projection onto the n-plane P.plane = range p; it is linear (p = P.projectionLinearMap), symmetric (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric) and idempotent (Grassmannian.project_project). A set S ⊆ ℝ^N is an L-Lipschitz graph over P when |(y − z) − p(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ S; every subset of such a set is again one. Write C := ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2}), μ := H^n and, for a ∈ ℝ^N, F(a) := Σ_{y∈A, p(y)=a} g(y), the [0,∞]-valued sum (tsum) of g over the subtype {y : y ∈ A ∧ p(y) = a}.

1. Preliminaries. p is injective on A: if y, z ∈ A and p(y) = p(z), then p(y − z) = 0 and the graph inequality forces y − z = 0. P.plane = range p is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed and Borel (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), and p(y) ∈ P.plane for every y.

2. Pieces of a simple function. Fix a Borel simple function s : ℝ^N → [0,∞] (MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc; its values may be ∞) with s ≤ g pointwise. For each c in the finite range of s put E_c := s⁻¹{c} (Borel) and A_c := E_c ∩ A. Each A_c ⊆ A is an L-Lipschitz graph over P and is H^n-null-measurable (a Borel set intersected with a null-measurable one). By graph_projection_null_measurable, p(A_c) is H^n-null-measurable; by graph_hausdorff_bound, μ(A_c) ≤ C·μ(p(A_c)).

3. The simple integral over A. By the definition of the integral of a simple function with respect to the restricted measure μ⌞A (SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) = Σ_c c·(μ⌞A)(s⁻¹{c})) and Measure.restrict_apply for the Borel sets E_c, SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) = Σ_c c·(μ⌞A)(E_c) = Σ_c c·μ(A_c). (No measurability of A is needed for this identity.)

4. Transfer to the plane. For each c, c·μ(A_c) ≤ c·C·μ(p(A_c)) = C·∫⁻ c·1_{p(A_c)} dμ, the equality by lintegral_indicator_const₀ (p(A_c) is null-measurable by step 2). Summing over the finite range and using finite additivity of the integral for the a.e.-measurable functions c·1_{p(A_c)} (lintegral_finsetSum', AEMeasurable.indicator₀): Σ_c c·μ(A_c) ≤ C·Σ_c ∫⁻ c·1_{p(A_c)} dμ = C·∫⁻ Φ dμ, where Φ(a) := Σ_c c·1_{p(A_c)}(a).

5. Pointwise comparison with the fibre sum: Φ(a) ≤ 1_{P.plane}(a)·F(a) for every a ∈ ℝ^N. (i) If a ∉ p(A), then a ∉ p(A_c) for every c (as A_c ⊆ A), so Φ(a) = 0. (ii) If a = p(y₀) with y₀ ∈ A, then for every c: a ∈ p(A_c) iff s(y₀) = c (if a = p(y) with y ∈ A_c ⊆ A, injectivity gives y = y₀ and so s(y₀) = c; conversely y₀ ∈ A_c when s(y₀) = c). Hence Φ(a) = Σ_c [s(y₀) = c]·c = s(y₀), because s(y₀) lies in the range of s (Finset.sum_ite_eq). Moreover s(y₀) ≤ g(y₀) ≤ F(a), since y₀ is one term of the fibre {y ∈ A : p(y) = a} (ENNReal.le_tsum), and a = p(y₀) ∈ P.plane.

6. Bound for s. By steps 3–5, lintegral_mono (which needs no measurability) and lintegral_indicator for the Borel set P.plane: SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) = Σ_c c·μ(A_c) ≤ C·∫⁻ Φ dμ ≤ C·∫⁻ 1_{P.plane}·F dμ = C·∫⁻_{P.plane} F dμ.

7. Arbitrary g. By definition (MeasureTheory.lintegral), the lower Lebesgue integral ∫⁻_A g dμ = ∫⁻ g d(μ⌞A) is the supremum of SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) over all Borel simple functions s ≤ g (rw [MeasureTheory.lintegral]; iSup₂_le). Each of these is at most C·∫⁻_{P.plane} F dμ by step 6, so ∫⁻_A g dH^n ≤ ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2})·∫⁻_{P.plane} (Σ_{y∈A, p(y)=a} g(y)) dH^n(a). No layer-cake formula is needed, and simple functions taking the value ∞ are allowed. ∎
proof_key_steps: p is injective on A and P.plane = range p is Borel.
For a Borel simple s ≤ g with level sets E_c: A_c := E_c ∩ A has μ(A_c) ≤ C μ(p(A_c)) and p(A_c) null-measurable (siblings).
SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) = Σ_c c μ(A_c) ≤ C ∫⁻ Σ_c c·1_{p(A_c)} dμ.
Pointwise Σ_c c·1_{p(A_c)}(a) ≤ 1_{P.plane}(a)·Σ_{y∈A, p(y)=a} g(y), by injectivity of p on A and s ≤ g.
Take the supremum over Borel simple s ≤ g (definition of the lower integral).
